qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Unrivaled branded jewellery duopoly (Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels) supported by centuries of Lindy heritage and protected designs (Love, Trinity, Alhambra). Pricing power proven by 4-8% regular annual price hikes with zero volume churn, generating 17-21% multi-cycle ROIC.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Premier hard luxury and branded jewellery duopoly (Cartier, Van Cleef & Arpels) possessing centuries-old Lindy heritage and unmatched pricing power. YNAP divestment cleanly prunes the e-commerce drag, refocusing capital on high-ROIC Jewellery Maisons. Balance sheet fortress with over €8.2B in net cash. [5-10Y g: branded jewellery volume 3.5% + luxury pricing power 3.5% + retail expansion mix 1.0% - watch cycle drag 0.5% + dividends/buybacks 1.0%]
qualitative.evidence: Compagnie Financière Richemont SA generates ~€20B+ in revenue, with Jewellery Maisons (Cartier, Van Cleef & Arpels, Buccellati) accounting for ~70% of sales and ~85% of operating profit at 30%+ operating margins. Operating ROIC has averaged 17-21% over the past four years (FY22: 15.4%, FY23: 21.1%, FY24: 19.4%, FY25: 17.7%). Net cash stood at €8.26B at FY2025 year-end with zero net debt. Branded fine jewellery benefits from a secular mix shift away from unbranded items, with Cartier and VCA wielding pricing power to raise prices 4-8% annually above inflation without sacrificing volume.
